item.title: Weeding out mutant deer
item.description: Kevin Copeland needs to reduce the fallow deer population on his patch of East Sussex, and especially a mutant strain that is throwing up murder bucks. Once Kevin has a deer on the ground, his friend Graham Payne steps in with his stalking horse – Tyson the cob, who is happy to carry the carcase back to the larder.See more of Tyson at https://www.instagram.com/thestalkingcob/

item.title: Fieldsports Britain – Sussex stalking horse
item.description: Pony power – we are out culling fallow deer in East Sussex with the aid of a beer-swilling cob. Plus, how bursting into song could help you regain your concentration at the clay ground. Our podcast this week features the woman who brought black bears back to Louisiana – and says they need shooting. Plus David has the news on the news stump. It’s all in this week’s #FieldsportsBritain

item.title: Clay Connections
item.description: Rob Ward-Dutton and Simon Sutton run a business-networking-fun-shooting club called Clay Connections. Currently in the North-West of England, they have ambitions to expand it across the UK. For more, visit https://clayconnections.co.uk/

item.title: How to bring back bears and wolves – FieldsportsChannel podcast, episode 137
item.description: What’s it like reintroducing a large predator to the wild? One person with firsthand experience is Maria Davidson, who manages the large carnivore programme for Safari Club International. She comes from the Louisiana Department of Fish and Wildlife, which has an impressive track record reintroducing black bears – as long as we can hunt them. She talks to Charlie Jacoby at the 2026 SCI Convention in Nashville.

item.title: Rooks, crows and jackies with Rob Speed
item.description: Spring crow shooting can be difficult. The birds are hungry but they have had a whole winter to build up wisdom and, today, the weather is wet. Rob Speed from @fieldsportswithspeed shows how he sets out to approach corvids on a field of spring drilling, with careful decoy patterns and – says Rob – 'hot snack of the day'.For more about the products featured in this video, follow these links:Browning https://browning.eu/Eley cartridges https://www.eleyhawkltd.com/Jack Pyke https://www.jackpyke.co.

item.title: Bill Blacker on the British gun trade – FieldsportsChannel podcast, episode 139
item.description: Doyen of the barrellers Bill Blackes is part of the beating heart of the British gun trade. He joines Charlie on the stage at the Carter Jones Game Fair Theatre to discuss his work and wider issues, such as how to cope with the forthcoming UK restrictions on lead shot.

item.title: Fieldsports Britain – Spring crows
item.description: We are shooting spring corvids with the fabulous Rob Speed from the Fieldsports with Speed channel. Spring is in the air for newly-released beavers, too, which are galloping off to start a new life on a shoot in Bedfordshire. ‘Barreller to the privileged classes’ Bill Blacker explains how he got started in the gun trade, and David has the news on the news stump. It’s all in this week’s #FieldsportsBritain

item.title: Shooting estate releases beavers
item.description: Gamekeeper Paul Dunn is helping release beavers at Southill in Bedfordshire. It’s all part of a conservation plan that will help secure the future of a wild bird shoot on the estate.To find out more about the Southill Estate, and the work of Restore, visit https://www.SouthillEstate.co.uk/ and https://RestoredLand.com/

item.title: Spring pigeon decoying, with Geoff Garrod
item.description: Essex gamekeeper and pigeonshooter Geoff Garrod is in clover– literally. He is shooting pigeons in a field of the stuff, after a winter when the birds mysteriously disappeared for months. He is using his favourite Eley cartridges in his 5-shot FAC Browning Maxus.To find your nearest stockist of Eley cartridges, visit Eley's dealer page at EleyHawkLtd.com/dealersFor more about Browning shotguns, go to Browning.euGeoff’s channel on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@GeoffGarrodShooting

item.title: Fieldsports Britain – shooting pigeons in clover
item.description: Geoff Garrod is in clover – he is back on the pigeons, after a winter when the birds mysteriously disappeared for months. Gun licensing woes: one police force has taken the law into its own hands and banned semi-auto shotguns from FACs. And how tech is catching up on grey squirrels: soon they will have to cope with facial recognition. Plus David has the news on the news stump. It’s all in this week’s #FieldsportsBritain

item.title: West Mercia Police make new gun laws
item.description: West Mercia Police has made up its own rules restricting Section 1 shotguns – that is shotguns with a magazine capacity greater than two cartridges, which are considered an essential everyday tool for pest controllers and gamekeepers. Their reason? Section 2 shotguns are sufficient for pest control, and Section 1 guns could be more dangerous if stolen. Gamekeeper Geoff Garrod explains why he needs a Section 1 shotgun to do his job.If you have been affected by the changes, please get in touch.

item.title: Facial recognition for squirrels
item.description: Ian Glendinning is working on a way to wipe out grey squirrels, using artificial intelligence, facial recognition and contraception. He is designing a camera that can track individual squirrels that visit a feeder – and dispense the pill to them.Contact Ian via the Red Squirrel Survival Trust https://www.rsst.org.uk/ian-glendinning/
